title: Using jo and desto for Proportional Change
goal: Use jo ... desto and jo ... jo to say that one change increases or decreases with another.

objectives.statement: Use jo ... desto and jo ... jo to say that one change increases or decreases with another.

spans.value: Maja and Henrik are planning a kitchen renovation. They have received several offers, but they still have not chosen a supplier.
Jo lenger vi venter, desto senere blir kjøkkenet ferdig.

blocks.translation: The longer we wait, the later the kitchen will be finished.

spans.value: Det er sant. Men jo fortere vi bestemmer oss, jo større er risikoen for at vi velger feil.

blocks.translation: That is true. But the faster we decide, the greater the risk is that we will make the wrong choice.

spans.value: Jo flere tilbud vi sammenligner, desto lettere blir det å velge.

blocks.translation: The more offers we compare, the easier it will be to choose.

spans.value: Kanskje. Jo mer jeg ser på prisene, desto mindre sikker blir jeg.

blocks.translation: Maybe. The more I look at the prices, the less certain I become.

spans.value: Da sammenligner vi de tre beste i kveld. Jo tidligere vi sender bestillingen, jo bedre.

blocks.translation: Then we’ll compare the three best ones tonight. The earlier we send the order, the better.

spans.value: Maja and Henrik are not merely listing separate facts. Each statement links two changing things. Waiting longer leads to later completion. Comparing more offers makes choosing easier. Looking at more prices makes Henrik less certain.
Norwegian commonly expresses this relationship with the paired patterns
jo ... desto
and
jo ... jo
The Norwegian construction corresponds closely to English
the more ..., the more ...
the less ..., the better ...
, and similar expressions.
Its two main forms are:

no.value: Jo mer vi planlegger, desto mindre tid kaster vi bort.

en.value: The more we plan, the less time we waste.

no.value: Jo mer vi planlegger, jo mindre tid kaster vi bort.

en.value: The more we plan, the less time we waste.

spans.value: Both patterns express the same basic proportional relationship.
Jo ... desto
is a clear and common pairing, while
jo ... jo
is also natural and frequent. The second
jo
does not introduce a new meaning; it fills the same role as
desto
in this construction.
The words following
jo
desto
, and the second
jo
normally contain a comparative form (
komparativ
A compact model is:
Jo + comparative change 1, desto/jo + comparative change 2.

no.value: Jo mer du øver, desto tryggere blir du.

en.value: The more you practise, the more confident you become.

no.value: Jo mindre vi kjøper, jo mer sparer vi.

en.value: The less we buy, the more we save.

spans.value: The two changes may move in the same direction:

no.value: Jo lenger hun arbeider med teksten, desto bedre blir den.

en.value: The longer she works on the text, the better it becomes.

spans.value: They may also move in opposite directions:

no.value: Jo høyere renta blir, desto færre boliger har vi råd til.

en.value: The higher the interest rate becomes, the fewer homes we can afford.

spans.value: The construction does not have to describe an exact mathematical rule. It presents a general relationship: as one thing changes, another tends to change too.

no.value: Jo bedre jeg kjenner byen, desto lettere finner jeg fram.

en.value: The better I know the city, the more easily I find my way around.

spans.value: This does not claim that every extra day in the city produces a measurable improvement. It expresses a recognizable connection between familiarity and ease.
The part beginning with the first
jo
establishes the condition or scale that changes.

no.value: Jo mer du leser ...

en.value: The more you read ...

no.value: Jo tidligere vi drar ...

en.value: The earlier we leave ...

no.value: Jo færre ting hun tar med ...

en.value: The fewer things she brings ...

spans.value: Because this part has subordinate-clause word order, the subject normally comes before the finite verb:

no.value: Jo mer du leser ...

en.value: The more you read ...

no.value: Jo tidligere vi drar ...

en.value: The earlier we leave ...

no.value: Jo mer leser du ...

en.value: The more read you ...

spans.value: The comparative expression can be one word or a longer phrase:

no.value: Jo dyrere maten blir ...

en.value: The more expensive the food becomes ...

no.value: Jo flere detaljer vi legger til ...

en.value: The more details we add ...

no.value: Jo mindre tid jeg har om morgenen ...

en.value: The less time I have in the morning ...

spans.value: Notice that
jo
is followed by the comparative information, not necessarily by the subject.

no.value: Jo større leilighet de kjøper ...

en.value: The larger the apartment they buy ...

spans.value: Here,
større leilighet
is the comparative expression. The subject
de
follows it.
The second part begins with
desto
or another
jo
and states the corresponding change.

no.value: Jo mer du leser, desto større blir ordforrådet ditt.

en.value: The more you read, the larger your vocabulary becomes.

no.value: Jo tidligere vi drar, jo mindre trafikk møter vi.

en.value: The earlier we leave, the less traffic we encounter.

spans.value: When the second part begins with a comparative expression, Norwegian uses main-clause verb-second order. The finite verb comes before the subject:

no.value: desto større blir ordforrådet ditt

en.value: the larger your vocabulary becomes

no.value: jo mindre trafikk møter vi

en.value: the less traffic we encounter

spans.value: Compare the two parts:

no.value: Jo mer du leser, desto lettere blir teksten.

en.value: The more you read, the easier the text becomes.

spans.value: This contrast is easy to miss because English does not show the same change.
A common mistake is to keep subject–verb order in the second part:

no.value: Jo mer du leser, desto lettere teksten blir.

en.value: The more you read, the easier the text becomes.

spans.value: Use:

no.value: Jo mer du leser, desto lettere blir teksten.

en.value: The more you read, the easier the text becomes.

spans.value: The same order appears with
jo ... jo

no.value: Jo lenger vi venter, jo dyrere blir reisen.

en.value: The longer we wait, the more expensive the trip becomes.

no.value: Jo mer hun forklarer, jo mindre forstår jeg.

en.value: The more she explains, the less I understand.

sections.title: Choosing jo ... desto or jo ... jo

spans.value: In most ordinary contexts, either pairing can express the intended relationship.

no.value: Jo nærmere vi kommer sentrum, desto dyrere blir hotellene.

en.value: The closer we get to the city centre, the more expensive the hotels become.

no.value: Jo nærmere vi kommer sentrum, jo dyrere blir hotellene.

en.value: The closer we get to the city centre, the more expensive the hotels become.

spans.value: The first
jo
remains fixed. The second marker may be
desto
or
jo
Do not combine them in the same second part:

no.value: Jo nærmere vi kommer sentrum, desto jo dyrere blir hotellene.

en.value: The closer we get to the city centre, the more expensive the hotels become.

spans.value: Very short versions are also common when the missing meaning is obvious:

no.value: Jo før, jo bedre.

en.value: The sooner, the better.

no.value: Jo mer, desto bedre.

en.value: The more, the better.

spans.value: These compact expressions follow the same pattern, even though the verbs and subjects are understood from context.
Compare a simple sequence of facts with a proportional statement:

no.value: Vi venter lenger. Reisen blir dyrere.

en.value: We wait longer. The trip becomes more expensive.

no.value: Jo lenger vi venter, desto dyrere blir reisen.

en.value: The longer we wait, the more expensive the trip becomes.

spans.value: The first version gives two facts. The second explicitly presents the higher price as connected with the longer wait.
Similarly:

no.value: Jeg bruker mindre tid på telefonen. Jeg får gjort mer.

en.value: I spend less time on my phone. I get more done.

no.value: Jo mindre tid jeg bruker på telefonen, jo mer får jeg gjort.

en.value: The less time I spend on my phone, the more I get done.

spans.value: When building such a sentence, ask two questions:

items.value: What is the first changing scale?
What happens to the second scale as the first changes?

spans.value: Then place each comparative expression immediately after its marker.

no.value: Jo flere spørsmål studentene stiller, desto tydeligere blir forklaringen.

en.value: The more questions the students ask, the clearer the explanation becomes.

spans.value: First scale: number of questions. Second scale: clarity of the explanation.

no.value: Jo mindre bagasje vi tar med, jo enklere blir reisen.

en.value: The less luggage we bring, the easier the journey becomes.

spans.value: First scale: amount of luggage. Second scale: ease of travel.
Do not replace the comparative with an ordinary positive form:

no.value: Jo mye du øver, desto god blir du.

en.value: The much you practise, the good you become.

spans.value: Use comparative forms:

no.value: Jo mer du øver, desto bedre blir du.

en.value: The more you practise, the better you become.

spans.value: An
enn
phrase is not normally needed. The sentence compares changing degrees, not one person or object directly with another.

no.value: Jo raskere hun går, desto varmere blir hun.

en.value: The faster she walks, the warmer she becomes.

no.value: Jo raskere enn hun går, desto varmere blir hun.

en.value: The faster than she walks, the warmer she becomes.

spans.value: That evening, Maja and Henrik compare their three preferred offers.
Jo nøyere jeg leser tilbudene, desto tydeligere blir forskjellene.

blocks.translation: The more carefully I read the offers, the clearer the differences become.

spans.value: Og jo flere ekstra kostnader vi finner, jo mindre attraktivt blir det billigste tilbudet.

blocks.translation: And the more additional costs we find, the less attractive the cheapest offer becomes.

spans.value: Jo færre endringer vi ber om, desto raskere kan firmaet bli ferdig.

blocks.translation: The fewer changes we request, the sooner the company can finish.

spans.value: Da velger vi det enkleste opplegget. Jo enklere planen er, jo lettere blir det å holde budsjettet.

blocks.translation: Then we’ll choose the simplest arrangement. The simpler the plan is, the easier it will be to stay within budget.

spans.value: Their decision now depends on several proportional relationships:

items.value: More careful reading produces clearer differences.
More extra costs make the cheapest offer less attractive.
Fewer requested changes allow earlier completion.
A simpler plan makes the budget easier to maintain.

spans.value: The grammar lets them compress each relationship into one connected statement.
Imagine that Nora and Elias are arranging a weekend train journey. Ticket prices are rising, early trains are less crowded, and carrying more luggage makes changing trains harder.

criteria.instruction: The message draws on the supplied renovation facts and does not contradict any of them; using one or more of the three relationships is sufficient.

The response is a Norwegian message addressed appropriately to Maja and Henrik for the purpose of helping them choose.
The message uses jo ... desto or jo ... jo to connect proportional changes described in the prompt.
If a target correlative appears, its first- and second-clause word order is accurate.

prompt.value: Velg en naturlig første del av setningen.
